subject: Urban Planning
title: Exclusionary Zoning and Race
description: A quick, practical guide to Exclusionary Zoning and Race.

hook.text: In 1917, the Supreme Court banned racial zoning. Cities responded by creating economic zoning that achieved the same result.

buildup.text: Banning apartments, requiring large lots, and mandating expensive construction materials priced out minorities.

discovery.text: Zoning didn't mention race. But planners knew exactly which communities these rules would exclude.

twist.text: Richard Rothstein's 'The Color of Law' documented how zoning was systematically used for racial segregation.

climax.text: Today, exclusionary zoning maintains segregation without ever using racial language. The mechanism is price.

punchline.text: Ban race from the law. Use price instead. Same result.

quiz.question: How did cities maintain racial segregation after racial zoning was banned?
options: They built walls between neighborhoods of different races
They used economic requirements like lot sizes and building standards as proxies
They assigned residents to neighborhoods based on employment location
